home.tagline: Every block can hold a world.
home.intro: A Fabric mod for Minecraft 26.3. Ten worlds, each sealed inside a single block and nested in the one before it. Every world has its own rule, its own creatures, its own station, and a boss guarding the core that opens the next.
home.facts: Minecraft 26.3 on Fabric, version 0.1.0. Solo and multiplayer.
home.dollsTitle: A set of eleven nesting dolls, just opened: the Surface, then worlds 1 to 10, from the largest to the smallest
home.dollsCaption: The Surface, then the ten worlds it holds. Pick a doll to open its world.
home.loopP: One loop, ten times over. Each pass asks you to unlearn the last world.

loop.p: Follow the Scroll's sketch to the Guardian's Sanctuary and beat the Block Guardian. It drops its core, the Matrix Workbench and your first World Soil.
At the Matrix Workbench: the last boss's core plus resources from its world. The World 1 Seed asks for the Guardian Core, 16 iron ingots and 16 oak logs.
Till World Soil with a hoe and plant the Seed. Each Seed wants the soil of the world before it, and one condition: water, heat, redstone, open sky, darkness, height.
The Seed hatches into a World Block. Use it and you shrink inside, onto a Threshold that brings you back out.
Toxin, heat, wind, noise, gravity, pressure: each world changes how you play. Its station turns local resources into the gear that answers the rule.

loop.h: Beat the boss, take its core
loop.p: Every attack is announced, then leaves an opening. Read the pattern, punish the opening, take the core.
The core is the key ingredient of the next Seed. Ten times, until the last block opens onto something much larger.

home.worldsP: Learning, then mastery, then expertise. World 10 tests everything at once.
home.sysP: Death teaches. It does not erase hours of progress.

systems.p: A nested doll you wear. When you die, a layer breaks instead and you get back up. It gains layers after Worlds 1, 5 and 8.
Every item holds a soul. At the Soul Altar, purify it for karma or devour it for power. Karma moves prices, quests and the ending.
Every weapon, tool and armour piece is born with one of six classes. Raise it to level 5 with souls, or gamble on a Chance Doll.
Up to eight players share a group, its worlds and its defeated bosses. Bosses grow tougher with every player who joins the fight.

home.desc: Matriochka, a Fabric mod for Minecraft 26.3: ten nested worlds, each sealed in a block, each with its own rule and boss.

worlds.lead: Each world is planted inside the one before it, and each one bends a rule you thought you knew. Numbers below come straight from the mod's code.
worlds.desc: The ten worlds of Matriochka: rules, Seeds, stations, recipes, creatures, bosses and structures.
worlds.noShot: No clear capture of this world yet: its signature block stands in.

bestiary.lead: Fifty creatures, five per world. Health and damage already include the world's multiplier: health grows by 35% and damage by 20% with every world you go down.
bestiary.nesting: Nesting creatures split open when they die and release a smaller, faster one. Elites guard the world's best drops.
bestiary.peoplesP: Every world has its own people, with villages, traders and quest givers. How they greet you depends on your karma. On the Surface, the Doll Peddler wanders between villages.
bestiary.desc: Every creature of Matriochka with its health, damage, behaviour and drops.

bosses.lead: Eleven fights, each built the same way: an announcement you can read, a fast and dangerous attack, then an opening. Hit a boss during its opening and it takes 1.5 times the damage; outside of it, only three quarters.
bosses.tierNote: Bosses never take damage while changing phase. The Spore Queen's cocoon holds until its nodes are broken.
bosses.mpNote: Counted within 48 blocks when the boss wakes. Everyone within 64 blocks at its death shares the victory.
bosses.rewardNote: plus 100 souls for every player in the fight
bosses.desc: The eleven bosses of Matriochka: health, attacks, phases, timings and rewards.

systems.lead: What keeps you alive, what you trade for power, and how your gear grows. Everything here works the same in solo and on a server.
systems.desc: Doll of Life, death and respawn, souls and karma, gear classes, groups and quests in Matriochka.

lifeDoll.p: You carry a doll made of layers. It gets its first layer when the Spore Queen falls, a second after the Light Eater and a third after the Master of Seasons. Every boss you beat restores one layer, and the Soul Altar rebuilds one for 50 souls.

death: If your Doll of Life has a layer left, it breaks and you get back up on the spot. A doll can save you at most once a minute.
Otherwise you die, and a death chest keeps your inventory where you fell. It never despawns; inside a boss arena it waits at the entrance.
If you placed a charged Soul Cradle in that world, you wake up next to it.
If not, you are sent back outside, to your usual spawn point.

features.p: A small painted cradle that lets you respawn inside a world. It holds 3 charges; feed it one resource from that world and 5 souls to add another. One active cradle per player and per world.
Pulls you back to the World Block. You can also simply walk back onto the Threshold where you arrived.

Break a World Block and everyone inside is pushed out safely. The block becomes a Cracked Doll tied to that exact world: set it down again and the world comes back with its bases and chests, unstable for 20 minutes. It is also how you move a world.

systems.soulsLead: Every item carries a soul whose weight depends on its rarity. Put it on the Soul Altar and choose, for good: purify it to free the soul and gain karma, or devour it to absorb the soul and lose karma. Either way you keep the souls, which pay for class upgrades, cradle charges and doll layers.
systems.karmaNote: Karma runs from −100 to +100. An item gives one point of karma per 10 souls, and less each time you repeat the same offering. Quests with a choice move it by 5 or 10.

karma.p: The peoples welcome you. Mutual-help quests open up and the brighter world variants answer you.
Prices are 10% lower. People trust you.
Neither saint nor devourer. Every choice still counts.
Prices are 10% higher, but the first black market opens to you.
Some villages turn hostile. Pact quests and forbidden loot await.

systems.karmaEnd: At ±100, karma also tilts the variants of the worlds you open, and it decides between two of the three endings: seal the creature away, or absorb its power.
systems.classesLead: Every weapon, tool and armour piece gets a random class when it is crafted. The Class Table raises its level with souls; your progression caps how far you can go.
systems.upNote: Level 1 to 5 costs 400 souls per piece.

chance.p: Rerolls an item into a different class it can hold, and keeps its level. The first reroll costs 20 souls, and the price doubles each time on the same item: 20, 40, 80, 160.

systems.nestingLead: The name is the rule: something can always hold something else. These systems unlock as the story goes on.

nest.b: A chest that holds a smaller one
A defeated mob releases a smaller one

gates: Enchanting, anvils and the Nether open after World 2.
Diamonds come back in World 5: four Diamond Fragments make one at the Dark Altar.
Elytra stay grounded in Worlds 4, 6 and 9 until World 8 is done.
systems.groupsLead: A player alone is a group of one. Worlds, progression and permissions belong to the group: up to eight players by default. Each group gets its own 3,000 by 3,000 block parcel in every world, walled off from the others, and a World Block can only be used by its group.

cmds.d: Your group, its members and defeated bosses
Invite a player into your group

systems.serverNote: The mod runs on the server and on every client. All rules, damage and rewards are decided by the server; nothing needs an online account or service.
systems.journalLead: The Artisan's Scroll arrives on your first login and turns into the Journal when the Guardian falls. Its tabs track your objective, quests, karma and worlds. There are 64 optional quests (4 on the Surface, 6 per world) and 100 achievements, 10 per world, two of them hidden. Fifty Journal pages and ten hidden dolls are scattered through the worlds; nest the dolls in order and something smaller opens.

download.lead: Version 0.1.0 for Minecraft 26.3 on Fabric. Install it on the client to play solo, and on both server and clients to play together.

Animated models of bosses and creatures

steps: Download matriochka-0.1.0.jar from the GitHub releases.
Put it in your mods folder with Fabric API and GeckoLib.
Launch the Fabric profile and create a new world. The Artisan's Scroll is waiting in your inventory.
download.lunar: Matriochka is built on Fabric so that it can run on Lunar Client, whose mod loading relies on Fabric. Support for Minecraft 26.3 together with GeckoLib is still being confirmed there: if the mod does not load, play it with the official launcher or Prism Launcher on a Fabric profile in the meantime.
download.wiki: Recipes, step-by-step guides and answers to common questions live on the GitHub wiki.
download.early: Names, numbers and balance can still change between versions. Back up your worlds before updating, and report anything odd on the issue tracker.

worlds.name: The Surface
worlds.short: Iron is the ceiling. Find the Guardian.
worlds.long: You wake up on the Surface with the Artisan's Scroll and a sketched map. Progression stops at iron until you earn more: enchanting, anvils and the Nether answer only once World 2 is done, the End once World 8 is. The Guardian's Sanctuary waits a few hundred blocks from spawn. Use its altar to wake the Block Guardian.

nums.l: worlds before enchanting, anvils and the Nether

worlds.bossNote: It drops the Guardian Core, the Matrix Workbench and four World Soil 0. Your Scroll becomes the Artisan's Journal.

worlds.name: Toxic Jungle
worlds.short: The air poisons you. Water washes it off.
worlds.long: A toxin gauge rises by 1 every second you breathe the jungle air and falls by 2 in water or rain. At 50 you slow down, at 75 you weaken, at 100 it eats your health. A Filter Mask halves the gain, Root Broth halves it again for five minutes, and an Antidote takes 50 off at once.

nums.l: toxin while you breathe the air
toxin, and it eats your health

armor.text: 16 armour, 1 toughness, a 7-damage weapon at this tier.

worlds.name: Giant Veins
worlds.short: Lava and depth cook you slowly.
worlds.long: Heat climbs by 1 per second within three blocks of lava and by 0.5 below y 40. Higher up and away from lava it drops by 1, in water by 2. Past 50 you get hungry, past 75 your pickaxe drags, at 100 you burn. Each piece of the Thermal set cuts the gain by 12.5%, Cooling Water takes 50 off, Ice Bread slows it for five minutes.

seed.name: World 2 Seed
seed.cond: The seed wants heat: lava, magma or a campfire.

station.name: Ash Foundry
station.note: Keep the temperature in the green.

items.name: Giant Ore
items.effect: A whole vein in one block.

armor.text: 17 armour, 2 toughness, a 9-damage weapon at this tier. Halves heat gain.

worlds.name: Endless Dungeon
worlds.short: No sky, only halls. And the halls move.
worlds.long: There is no surface and no sky, only dungeon. Sealed doors give way to Dungeon Keys, made at the Jailer's Table once you have reproduced the lock pattern. Every five minutes the halls rearrange themselves, with a ten-second warning. Light is scarce, so bring your own.

nums.l: between two rearrangements of the halls

seed.name: World 3 Seed
seed.cond: The seed wants a redstone signal.

armor.text: 18 armour, 3 toughness, a 11-damage weapon at this tier.

worlds.name: Storm Archipelago
worlds.short: Gusts throw you off the islands.
worlds.long: Floating islands under a permanent storm. Every 30 seconds a gust hits anyone under the open sky unless they crouch or take shelter, and you hear it two seconds early. Every 45 seconds lightning marks a spot near exposed players with sparks, then strikes three seconds later. Elytra stay grounded here until the Master of Seasons falls: the Glider and the Grappling Hook are how you cross.

nums.l: from the sparks to the strike

seed.name: World 4 Seed
seed.cond: The seed wants the open sky.

station.name: Lightning Forge
station.note: Needs a lightning strike or storm essence.

armor.text: 19 armour, 4 toughness, a 13-damage weapon at this tier.

worlds.bossNote: It drops the Storm King Core.

worlds.name: Lightless Deep
worlds.short: Total darkness. Every step makes noise.
worlds.long: No light, and a noise gauge. Sprinting adds 4 per second, walking 0.6; standing still removes 1.5, sneaking 3. Above 50, every creature within 28 blocks comes for you. Darkness washes over your sight every ten seconds unless you carry a lit Solar Lantern (20 minutes of light) or night vision. Silence Balm wipes your noise.

nums.l: noise, and everything comes for you
blocks: how far they come from

armor.text: 20 armour, 6 toughness, a 16-damage weapon at this tier.

worlds.bossNote: It drops the Light Eater Core.

worlds.name: Upside Realm
worlds.long: Every 90 seconds gravity flips: you float upward for six seconds, then drift back down for twelve. A warning comes five seconds before. Gravity Boots ignore the flip entirely; a Stabilizer or a Flipped Apple keeps you steady for 30 seconds.

station.name: Inverter
station.note: Every gain comes with a flaw.

armor.text: 22 armour, 8 toughness, a 19-damage weapon at this tier.

worlds.name: Pressure Ocean
worlds.short: Your oxygen runs out. The pressure crushes.
worlds.long: Under water you breathe from your own oxygen gauge: about 50 seconds without a suit, five minutes in the full Diving set. Surfacing refills 10 per second. Below y 110 the pressure starts to crush you; the full Diving set pushes that limit down to y 40. Oxygen Capsules and Apnea Kelp buy time, the Thruster brings you back up fast.

armor.text: 24 armour, 10 toughness, a 23-damage weapon at this tier. Resists pressure.

worlds.name: Hastened Seasons
worlds.short: A day lasts eight minutes. A season, two.
worlds.long: Time runs three times faster: a full day and night take eight minutes, each season two. Summer leaves you hungry, winter slows you down, spring and autumn are your windows. A Season Preserve shields you for two minutes, the Hourglass holds the clock for 90 seconds, and the Time Workshop only accepts recipes at dawn and dusk.

seed.name: World 8 Seed
seed.cond: The seed hatches at dawn or dusk.

station.name: Time Workshop
station.note: Accepts recipes at dawn and dusk.

armor.text: 26 armour, 12 toughness, a 28-damage weapon at this tier.

worlds.name: Restless Ground
worlds.long: Every 60 seconds the ground heaves: you are thrown and nauseous, and up to four loose blocks around you collapse. You get three seconds of warning. Within 16 blocks of a Terrain Anchor nothing moves; an Anchor in hand steadies you for ten minutes, and Grip Boots keep you on your feet.

nums.l: blocks of calm around a Terrain Anchor

seed.name: World 9 Seed

armor.text: 28 armour, 14 toughness, a 33-damage weapon at this tier.

worlds.name: The Giant Workshop
worlds.short: Every old rule, in a workshop built for giants.
worlds.long: You step out of the last block into a workshop built for giants, where your own base sits on a workbench like an object. The world is cut into nine zones of 256 blocks, each running the rule of one earlier world, from toxin to tremors. Every piece of old gear earns its place again.

nums.l: zones, each with an earlier rule

seed.name: World 10 Seed
seed.cond: The seed is ready. It only waits for you.

armor.text: 30 armour, 16 toughness, a 40-damage weapon at this tier.
